questions.question: Explain how acid mine drainage forms and what harm it does, describe how dust from mine dumps affects nearby communities, and state the remedies for each.
questions.expected_answer: Witwatersrand gold reefs contain pyrite; mining exposed it to air and water, and when mines closed and pumping stopped the workings flooded, so water and oxygen reacting with pyrite formed sulphuric acid that dissolved iron, aluminium, manganese and traces of uranium and other metals. The acid water rose and decanted at the surface, as on the West Rand in 2002, running orange into streams feeding the Crocodile and Vaal systems and the Cradle of Humankind's dolomite, killing aquatic life, corroding concrete and steel, making water unfit for drinking and irrigation and depositing metals in soil; the remedy is pumping and treating with lime to neutralise acid and settle metals, at plants built from 2012 at great and ongoing public cost. Mine dumps and slimes dams of finely crushed tailings are dry, fine and often bare, and wind lifts their dust, carrying silica and in gold tailings low-level uranium, into adjacent townships such as Soweto, Riverlea and Snake Park, causing asthma, chest infections and eye irritation; remedies are vegetating or spraying dumps, reprocessing them to remove them, and not building settlements beside them.

questions.question: Describe how iron was mined and smelted in South Africa before the modern era, naming sites and periods, and explain why indigenous knowledge is studied in Technology.
questions.expected_answer: From about the third century of the common era, Iron Age farming communities in Limpopo, Mpumalanga, KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng mined surface iron ores such as haematite, magnetite and laterite and smelted them in clay shaft furnaces a metre or more high, charged with alternating layers of charcoal and crushed ore and blown through clay tuyeres by skin bellows; the carbon stripped oxygen from the ore to leave a bloom of iron that smiths hammered free of slag and forged into hoes, spear heads, axes, knives and ornaments. Sites include Mapungubwe, Phalaborwa, where copper and iron were worked for centuries, the Soutpansberg and the Tugela valley, with copper at Musina, tin at Rooiberg and gold traded from Mapungubwe and Great Zimbabwe to the coast by the thirteenth century. Indigenous knowledge is studied because it shows that technology, in the full sense of investigation, design, skilled making and evaluation by specialists, was developed in Africa long before colonisation, correcting a bias, and because its use of local renewable materials, human power and small-scale workings and its understanding of airflow and heat offer lessons to modern designers.

questions.question: Outline the history and present position of women in South African mining, define bias in technology with reference to the headgear project, and set out the shape of a balanced report.
questions.expected_answer: The Mines and Works Act of 1911 and later laws barred women from underground and most skilled work, reserving it for men and through the colour bar for white men, with black men recruited as migrant labour; women held few surface and clerical jobs until the ban was lifted in 1996 by the Mine Health and Safety Act, and the Mining Charter from 2004 set participation targets. Women are now about 15 to 20 percent of the mining workforce in roles from rock drill operator to winding engine driver and manager, but remain a minority, especially underground and in senior technical posts, and face barriers such as protective equipment designed for men, inadequate underground facilities, harassment, assumptions about strength and belonging, and rosters that conflict with family responsibilities. Bias in technology is design that assumes one kind of user and so excludes others; a headgear bid that assumes every cage occupant is a tall man builds that bias in, so cages, signalling and safety gear should suit a range of bodies. A balanced report states the question, gives dated and located background, presents cited evidence from at least three sources with numbers, gives more than one perspective such as mine, community, worker and regulator, reaches a conclusion the evidence supports, and recommends action including what the company's design will do, in about a page with a sketch, map or table and a source list.
